The Kantorovich linear program reformulates the Monge assignment problem into a convex optimization task by relaxing the point-to-point constraint to a joint distribution over product spaces. This duality allows for tractable numerical solutions using linear programming techniques. The entropic regularization introduces an information-theoretic penalty term that makes the problem differentiable and amenable to modern machine learning algorithms such as Sinkhorn iterations. The resulting regularized transport plan approximates the true optimal transport map while maintaining computational efficiency. The Wasserstein metric then defines a notion of distance between probability distributions based on this transport cost, forming a complete metric space. These primitives collectively enable GSI to model complex probabilistic dependencies and perform robust inference under uncertainty, while GSE uses these structures to encode dynamic decision-making processes involving evolving belief states.
